title: Lippan kaam mud-and-mirror relief
summary: In the Kutch region, women and men press a dough of clay and dung onto the walls of round houses, raise it into bands and medallions, and set small cut mirrors into it. When the lamp is lit the wall glitters.
howToPlay: The framed picture shows a finished clay panel with its mirrors.
Tap a square of the panel to set a mirror there; the same mirror appears at its partner places around the centre.
Tap a mirror again to take it out.
Press Check to see how close your panel is to the frame.
rules: The panel is built outwards from its middle, so every mirror you set is repeated in the four quarters and their reflections.
Keep a narrow border of clay around the design.
Three stars need a panel almost exactly like the frame.
heritageNote: Lippan kaam belongs to Kutch in Gujarat, India, with related work in Sindh, Pakistan. Clay mixed with dung is worked by hand into raised patterns on house walls, which also helps to insulate them, and small mirrors catch the lamplight. Communities such as the Rabari and the Mutwa each keep their own styles, and some avoid drawing people or animals.
